t: April–May 2004: India held its 14th Lok Sabha general elections in four phases, using electronic voting machines fully nationwide for the first time.

The "India Shining" Upset: The ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) called early elections, confident in their "India Shining" economic campaign. However, the alliance faced a shock defeat due to rising concerns over job scarcity and rural economic distress.
Sonia Gandhi’s Renunciation: In May, despite leading the Congress-led United Progressive Alliance (UPA) to victory, Sonia Gandhi stunned the nation by declining the Prime Ministership.
Dr. Manmohan Singh Sworn In: On May 22, 2004, renowned economist Dr. Manmohan Singh was sworn in as India's 13th Prime Minister, heading the new UPA coalition government.
State Assemblies: Regional shifts took place as the Congress party won major state elections, notably forming a new government under Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy in Andhra Pradesh.
A massive 9.1 magnitude earthquake off the coast of Sumatra, Indonesia, triggered a catastrophic tsunami across the Indian Ocean.
Devastation: The tsunami struck India’s southeastern coast and islands with wave heights reaching up to 12 meters. Over 10,000 people were killed, and thousands more went missing or were displaced.
Impacted Regions: The Union Territory of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, alongside mainland coastal areas in Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Pondicherry, suffered the worst brunt of the disaster.

September 2004: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) successfully launched GSAT-3, popularly known as EDUSAT. It was the first Indian satellite built exclusively to service the educational sector, bringing interactive distance classroom environments to remote and rural areas.

Indo-Pak Peace Process: In June, after bilateral talks on nuclear confidence-building measures, India and Pakistan agreed to establish a dedicated hotline to avoid accidental nuclear risks and maintain a moratorium on nuclear testing.

Internal Security: Government operations led to a notable drop in militancy incidents in Jammu & Kashmir compared to the prior year. Meanwhile, domestic security focus shifted toward containing Naxalite operations across central and eastern states.

The End of Veerappan: On October 18, 2004, the notorious forest bandit and sandalwood smuggler, Koose Munisamy Veerappan, was shot dead by the Tamil Nadu Special Task Force in Operation Cocoon, ending a decades-long multi-state manhunt.

Kanchi Shankaracharya Arrest: In November, Jayendra Saraswathi, the prominent seer of the Kanchi Kamakoti Peetham, was arrested in connection with a high-profile murder case, sparking massive national media coverage and religious debate.

Historic Tour of Pakistan: In March and April, the Indian cricket team led by Sourav Ganguly visited Pakistan for a historic full-fledged cricket series. India won both the One Day International (ODI) series and clinched their first-ever Test series victory on Pakistani soil.
Olympic Silver: At the 2004 Athens Olympics, Major Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore won a Silver Medal in the men's double trap shooting event, securing India’s first-ever individual Olympic silver medal.
Right to Information (RTI) Act: Enacted in October 2005, giving ordinary citizens the legal power to request information from public authorities, radically boosting public transparency.
MGNREGA Enactment: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act was passed, legally guaranteeing 100 days of wage employment per year to rural households.
Value Added Tax (VAT): Introduced on April 1, 2005, across most Indian states to streamline domestic trade taxation.
Kashmir Bus Service: On April 7, the first bus service in 60 years commenced between Srinagar and Muzaffarabad across the Line of Control.
India–US Nuclear Pact: Initial frameworks and diplomatic dialogues were established, laying the foundation for the historic civil nuclear cooperation agreement.
The Great Mumbai Floods: In July 2005, unprecedented monsoon rains dumped 94 cm of precipitation within 24 hours, bringing the financial capital to a standstill and claiming hundreds of lives.
Mandher Devi Temple Stampede: A horrific stampede occurred in January in Maharashtra, leading to over 200 fatalities.
Kashmir Earthquake: On October 8, a catastrophic 7.6 magnitude earthquake hit the region, necessitating major cross-border disaster relief operations.
Valigonda Train Derailment: A flash flood washed away a bridge in Andhra Pradesh in October, causing a derailment that resulted in 77 fatalities.
Vadodara Train Crash: A severe collision between a passenger train and a goods train occurred in Gujarat.
Dadasaheb Phalke Award: Renowned director Adoor Gopalakrishnan was honored with India's highest cinema award.
IFFI Goa: The 36th International Film Festival of India was permanently institutionalized in Goa with veteran actor Dev Anand opening the event.
The cross-border Thar Express railway link between India and Pakistan is officially approved to resume operations after 41 years of disruption, serving as a key bilateral confidence-building measure.

The Government of India officially launches the landmark Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA). The law guarantees 100 days of wage employment per financial year to rural households, establishing one of the largest social security programs in human history.

U.S. President George W. Bush visits India. During the visit, a historic US-India Peaceful Atomic Energy Cooperation Act (the civil nuclear deal) is signed, effectively ending India's decades-long global nuclear isolation.
The Varanasi Bombings occur. A series of terrorist attacks strike the Sankat Mochan Hanuman Temple and Varanasi Cantonment railway station, killing at least 15 people and injuring over 50 others.
A massive fire breaks out at a consumer electronics fair in Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, resulting in the tragic deaths of over 100 people.

May: The 2006 Indian anti-reservation protests erupt. Led by medical students and doctors under the banner "Youth for Equality," nationwide strikes and rallies challenge the Union Government's decision to implement a 27% quota for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in premier higher education institutions.
The historic Nathu La Pass—a mountain pass in the Himalayas connecting Sikkim with Tibet—reopens for cross-border trade for the first time since the 1962 Sino-Indian War.

The 2006 Mumbai Train Bombings devastate the city's transit system. Seven serial explosions tear through the first-class compartments of the Mumbai Suburban Railway over a span of 11 minutes, killing 209 people and injuring more than 700.
A rare meteorite fall is recorded and witnessed across regions of Rajasthan.

July – September: Severe monsoon low-pressure systems cause massive prolonged flooding across Gujarat, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Andhra Pradesh, claiming over 1,700 lives nationwide.
The Malegaon Bombings occur. Three explosions rock a Muslim cemetery and mosque area in Malegaon, Maharashtra, during a religious festival, leaving upwards of 31 people dead.

October: Tata Steel acquires Anglo-Dutch steelmaker Corus for $12 billion. This marks the largest overseas corporate acquisition by an Indian company at the time, signaling the global rise of Indian multinational firms.
Cyclonic Storm Ogni makes landfall over Andhra Pradesh, causing severe localized flooding, agricultural destruction, and dozens of casualties.

The Indian Parliament enacts the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, legally recognizing the land and resource rights of forest-dwelling communities.
Literature: Author Kiran Desai wins the prestigious 2006 Man Booker Prize for her novel, The Inheritance of Loss.
Cinema: Major cinematic landmarks are released, including the socio-political phenomenon Rang De Basanti, the gritty Shakespearean adaptation Omkara, and the box-office juggernaut Dhoom 2.
Television: The Indian reality TV phenomenon Bigg Boss premieres its very first season in November.
Sports: Indian shooters dominate the Melbourne Commonwealth Games, securing 16 gold medals, while Abhinav Bindra wins the ISSF World Shooting Championships.
Severe flash floods and landslides struck Uttarakhand (June 15–17, 2013), causing catastrophic loss of life around Kedarnath and the Mandakini river basin.
Cyclone Phailin hit the coasts of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh in October, prompting a massive evacuation of over 1.3 million people.
An illegal seven-story building collapsed in Shil Phata, Thane (April 2013), killing 74 people.
Fatal stampedes occurred at the Allahabad railway station (February) and near the Ratangarh Mata Temple in Datia, Madhya Pradesh (October).
Serial blasts targeted a BJP rally in Patna addressed by Narendra Modi in October.
The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) successfully launched the Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) on November 5, 2013.
Parliament passed major reform legislation, including the National Food Security Act and the Land Acquisition Act.
The Union Cabinet cleared the creation of Telangana as India's 29th state in October 2013

A Historic Mandate: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) won a landslide victory, securing 282 seats independently. This marked the first time in 30 years that a single political party achieved a full majority without relying on a coalition.
New Leadership: On May 26, 2014, Narendra Modi was officially sworn in as the 15th Prime Minister of India, succeeding Dr. Manmohan Singh.

The Delhi Shuffle: Earlier in February, Arvind Kejriwal resigned as the Chief Minister of Delhi after a brief 49-day tenure following the deadlock over the Jan Lokpal Bill, plunging the capital into President's Rule before subsequent state elections.
India's 29th State: Following decades of intense localized struggle and the passing of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, Telangana officially became India's 29th state on June 2, 2014.
K. Chandrashekar Rao took charge as its very first Chief Minister, while Hyderabad was designated as the shared capital for both states for a transition period of up to ten years.

Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan): On September 24, 2014, India created global space history. The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) successfully inserted the Mangalyaan spacecraft into Martian orbit. India became the first nation in the world to successfully reach Mars on its very first attempt, and the first Asian country to do so.

Polio-Free India: In March 2014, the World Health Organization (WHO) officially certified India—and the entire South-East Asian region—as completely Polio-Free, celebrating a monumental victory for public health campaigns.

Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (August 28): A massive financial inclusion drive aimed at ensuring every single household in India has access to a bank account. Millions of zero-balance accounts were opened in record time.
Make in India (September 25): A global initiative launched to transform India into an international manufacturing hub, encouraging domestic production and inviting foreign investments.
Swachh Bharat Abhiyan (October 2): Launched on Mahatma Gandhi’s birth anniversary, this nationwide cleanliness campaign focused on eliminating open defecation and modernizing solid waste management.

NITI Aayog Announcement: On December 31, 2014, Prime Minister Modi announced the complete scrapping of the historic 65-year-old Planning Commission, replacing it with the NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India).

Recognition of the Third Gender: In a historic human rights ruling (National Legal Services Authority v. Union of India), the Supreme Court formally recognized transgender individuals as a distinct "third gender," safeguarding their constitutional rights.

Coal Allocation Scrapped: The Supreme Court sent shockwaves through the corporate sector by declaring the allocation of 214 coal blocks distributed between 1993 and 2010 completely illegal, forcing structural reforms in the energy sector.

Kashmir Floods (September): Catastrophic rains caused the Jhelum River to overflow, triggering the worst floods the region had seen in half a century. Hundreds lost their lives, and thousands were stranded before the Indian Armed Forces launched Operation Megh Rahat.

Cyclone Hudhud (October): A category-4 equivalent severe cyclonic storm battered the eastern coast, causing massive structural and agricultural damage in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, and parts of Odisha.

Nobel Peace Prize: Indian child rights activist Kailash Satyarthi was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize alongside Pakistan's Malala Yousafzai. Satyarthi was recognized for his decades of relentless work through the Bachpan Bachao Andolan, rescuing over 80,000 children from forced labor and trafficking.
The Government of India formally established the NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India), completely replacing the 65-year-old Planning Commission.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the flagship "Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao" (Save the Daughter, Educate the Daughter) and Sukanya Samriddhi Account welfare schemes.
US President Barack Obama attended India's Republic Day parade as the Chief Guest, marking the first time a US president filled this role.
India successfully test-fired its first canister-launched version of the Agni-V Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (ICBM) from Wheeler Island.
The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), led by Arvind Kejriwal, secured a historic landslide victory in the Delhi Legislative Assembly elections, winning 67 out of 70 seats.
The Supreme Court of India struck down Section 66A of the Information Technology Act, declaring it unconstitutional and protecting freedom of speech online.
Former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee was awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honor.
Saina Nehwal became the first Indian woman shuttler to attain the World No. 1 rank in badminton.
The Indian Armed Forces executed Operation Raahat, successfully evacuating over 4,640 Indian nationals and 960 foreign citizens from war-torn Yemen.
A massive 7.9-magnitude earthquake devastated Nepal, causing severe tremors across North and East India and resulting in cross-border casualties.
The Karnataka High Court acquitted Tamil Nadu Chief Minister J. Jayalalithaa in her long-running disproportionate assets case, paving the way for her political return.
India and Bangladesh signed a historic Land Boundary Agreement, ending a decades-old border dispute by exchanging 162 enclaves.
The First International Yoga Day was celebrated globally; PM Modi led a massive gathering of over 35,000 people at Rajpath in New Delhi.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi officially inaugurated the Digital India campaign to enhance online infrastructure and digital literacy.
Terrorists attacked a police station in Gurdaspur, Punjab, killing seven people before the three attackers were neutralized.
Former President and esteemed scientist Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam passed away at the age of 83 after collapsing during a lecture in Shillong.
ISRO successfully launched Astrosat, India's first dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory, using the PSLV-XL rocket.
October: Tensions escalated across the nation following the tragic Dadri lynching incident over rumors of beef possession, triggering widespread social debates.
The Mahagathbandhan (Grand Alliance) of JD(U) and RJD defeated the BJP-led alliance in the Bihar Legislative Assembly elections, returning Nitish Kumar as Chief Minister.
November – December: Unprecedented heavy monsoon rains triggered the catastrophic 2015 Chennai Floods, which claimed over 400 lives and caused billions in infrastructure damage.
In an impromptu diplomatic move, PM Modi made a surprise stopover in Lahore to meet Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif.
National Economy: The Union Budget abolished the wealth tax and increased service tax to 14%. GDP growth hit 7.3%.
Banking & Finance: Mudra Bank was launched to fund small businesses, and commercial licenses were granted to Bandhan Bank and IDFC.
Defense Reform: The government formally approved the implementation of the long-awaited One Rank, One Pension (OROP) scheme.
Demonetization: On November 8, 2016, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the demonetization of ₹500 and ₹1,000 banknotes to curb black money.
Uri Attack & Surgical Strikes: In September 2016, militants attacked an army camp in Uri, Jammu and Kashmir, killing 19 soldiers; India responded with surgical strikes across the Line of Control.
Pathankot Attack: Terrorists attacked the Indian Air Force base in Pathankot in January 2016.
Rio Olympics: PV Sindhu won a silver medal in badminton for India.
ISRO Launch: ISRO successfully launched multiple satellites using a single rocket.
Telecom Expansion: Reliance Jio launched its 4G telecom network with free/cheap promotional plans.
Passing of J. Jayalalithaa: Former Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, J. Jayalalithaa, passed away in December 2016
New Leadership (July-August): Ram Nath Kovind was elected as the 14th President of India, succeeding Pranab Mukherjee. Shortly after, M. Venkaiah Naidu was sworn in as the 13th Vice-President.

State Elections (March-December): The BJP expanded its political footprint significantly, securing a landslide victory in Uttar Pradesh (where Yogi Adityanath became Chief Minister), alongside wins in Uttarakhand, Goa, Manipur, Himachal Pradesh, and Gujarat. The Congress party won Punjab.
Cabinet Reshuffle (September): Nirmala Sitharaman was appointed as the Defence Minister, becoming only the second woman to hold the post after Indira Gandhi.

The GST Rollout (July 1): India launched the Goods and Services Tax (GST), executing the country's most significant indirect tax reform since independence by replacing a complex web of central and state taxes with a unified system.
Ease of Doing Business (October): Driven by structural changes, India jumped an unprecedented 30 spots to break into the top 100 in the World Bank’s Ease of Doing Business index.

Demonetization Aftermath: The economy experienced a brief deceleration in growth (dipping to a multi-year low of 5.7% in the mid-quarter) as small businesses and the automotive sector adjusted to the cash crunch from the late-2016 banknote ban.
Right to Privacy (August): A 9-judge bench of the Supreme Court unanimously declared the Right to Privacy as a Fundamental Right under Article 21 of the Constitution.
Triple Talaq Banned (August): The Supreme Court ruled the practice of instant triple talaq (Talaq-e-Biddat) unconstitutional and void.
Electoral Banning (January): The apex court prohibited the use of religion, race, caste, community, or language to seek votes during elections.
ISRO's World Record (February 15): The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) made history by successfully launching 104 satellites in a single mission using the PSLV-C37 rocket.

Inauguration of Mega Projects: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Chenani-Nashri Tunnel in Jammu & Kashmir (India's longest highway tunnel at the time) and Phase 1 of the high-tech Hyderabad Metro.

Doklam Standoff (June–August): A tense, 73-day military face-off occurred between Indian and Chinese armed forces over Chinese road construction in the Doklam plateau near the Bhutan border. It was successfully resolved via diplomatic withdrawal.
ICJ Victory (November): India scored a massive diplomatic win when judge Dalveer Bhandari was re-elected to the International Court of Justice after the UK withdrew its candidate.
Miss World 2017 (November): Manushi Chhillar won the Miss World pageant, bringing the blue crown back to India after a 17-year hiatus.
FIFA U-17 World Cup (October): India hosted its first-ever FIFA tournament, the FIFA U-17 World Cup, which catalyzed massive soccer infrastructure updates across major cities.

Entertainment & Weddings (December): The Indian film industry saw historical box-office records shattered by Baahubali 2: The Conclusion. In December, cricketer Virat Kohli and actor Anushka Sharma wed in Tuscany, Italy
Section 377 Decriminalized: In a historic verdict on September 6, the Supreme Court of India unanimously struck down the colonial-era law, decriminalizing consensual gay sex.

Aadhaar Verdict: The Supreme Court upheld the constitutional validity of Aadhaar but significantly limited its scope, declaring it unnecessary for bank accounts, school admissions, and mobile connections.
Sabarimala Verdict: The apex court ruled that women of all ages must be allowed entry into the Sabarimala temple in Kerala, stating that selective exclusion violates fundamental rights.
Judiciary Crisis: Four senior judges of the Supreme Court held an unprecedented press conference to air public grievances regarding the administration and allocation of cases by the Chief Justice.
Statue of Unity Inauguration: Prime Minister Narendra Modi unveiled the world's tallest statue (182 meters)—a monument dedicated to India’s first Home Minister, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, in Gujarat.
Farmers' Marches: Tens of thousands of farmers participated in massive protest marches across Mumbai and New Delhi, demanding farm loan waivers and fair crop pricing.
Renaming Drive: The Uttar Pradesh government executed a major renaming initiative, officially changing Allahabad to Prayagraj and Faizabad to Ayodhya.
ISRO Milestone: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) successfully launched its 100th satellite using the PSLV-C40 carrier vehicle.
Aviation History: Flying Officer Avani Chaturvedi became the first Indian woman to fly a fighter jet solo, piloting a MiG-21 Bison.

Walmart-Flipkart Acquisition: U.S. retail giant Walmart acquired a 77% controlling stake in Indian e-commerce pioneer Flipkart for $16 billion, marking the world's largest e-commerce acquisition at the time.
$100 Billion Milestones: Both Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) and Reliance Industries (RIL) crossed the elite $100 billion market capitalization threshold.
PNB Scam Uncovered: A massive multi-crore financial fraud involving celebrity jeweler Nirav Modi was unearthed at the Punjab National Bank.
Kerala Floods: During August, Kerala suffered its worst monsoon flooding in nearly a century, resulting in over 400 casualties and displacing hundreds of thousands of citizens.
Cyclone Gaja: A severe cyclonic storm hit the coastal regions of Tamil Nadu in November, causing heavy infrastructure damage and agricultural loss.
Under-19 Cricket World Cup: The Indian cricket team, coached by Rahul Dravid, clinical won the ICC U-19 World Cup in New Zealand.
Blind Cricket World Cup: India retained their title by defeating Pakistan in a thrilling final held in Sharjah.
Hima Das Sprint: Hima Das became the first Indian track athlete to win a gold medal at a global event during the World U20 Championships.
Atal Bihari Vajpayee: The former Prime Minister of India and co-founder of the BJP passed away on August 16.
M. Karunanidhi: The veteran DMK patriarch and former Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu passed away on August 7.
Sridevi: The legendary Indian cinema superstar passed away unexpectedly in Dubai on February 24.

10% EWS Reservation Approved (January 7): The Union Cabinet approved a 10% reservation quota in central government jobs and educational institutions for the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) among the general category.
The Pulwama Terror Attack (February 14): A suicide bomber targeted a convoy of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) in Pulwama, Jammu & Kashmir, resulting in the tragic loss of 40 jawans.
The Balakot Airstrike (February 26): In a retaliatory counter-terror operation, the Indian Air Force (IAF) conducted precision airstrikes on a Jaish-e-Mohammed training camp in Balakot, Pakistan.

Mission Shakti (March 27): India successfully conducted its first anti-satellite (A-SAT) missile test, destroying a live satellite in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) and becoming the fourth nation with this capability.
2019 Lok Sabha Elections (April 11 – May 19): India conducted the world's largest democratic exercise across seven polling phases, recording its highest-ever historical voter turnout.

Landslide Victory & Modi 2.0 (May 23): The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) won a decisive single-party majority with 303 seats (353 for the NDA alliance), securing a second consecutive term for Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Formation of Jal Shakti Ministry (May): The government consolidated its water-related administrative bodies into the single unified Ministry of Jal Shakti to streamline water management and launch the Jal Jeevan Mission.
Chandrayaan-2 Launch (July 22): The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) launched its second lunar exploration mission, featuring an orbiter, lander (Vikram), and rover (Pragyan).

Abrogation of Article 370 (August 5): The Parliament revoked the special status granted to Jammu & Kashmir under Article 370. The state was officially reorganized into two distinct Union Territories: Jammu & Kashmir, and Ladakh.
Banning of Triple Talaq (August 1): The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act was passed, officially criminalizing the practice of instant triple talaq.
Final Assam NRC List (August 31): The final National Register of Citizens (NRC) list for Assam was published, validating over 3 crore residents and excluding roughly 19 lakh people.
Corporate Tax Rate Cut (September 20): In a major boost to revive economic growth, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman slashed base corporate tax rates for domestic companies from 30% to 22%.

Opening of the Kartarpur Corridor (October 24): India and Pakistan signed a historic agreement to open a visa-free transit corridor, allowing Indian Sikh pilgrims access to the Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Pakistan.

The Ayodhya Verdict (November 9): A unanimous 5-judge bench of the Supreme Court resolved a decades-old land dispute, awarding the contested Ayodhya site to a trust for a Hindu temple and allocating an alternative 5 acres to the Sunni Waqf Board for a mosque.

Citizenship Amendment Act passed (December 11): Parliament passed the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA), offering an accelerated path to citizenship for persecuted religious minorities from Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Afghanistan, which sparked widespread nationwide protests.

Appointment of Chief of Defence Staff (December 30): The government created the post of Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) to ensure seamless tri-service integration, appointing General Bipin Rawat as India's first CDS.
Badminton History: P.V. Sindhu became the first Indian ever to win gold at the BWF Badminton World Championships by defeating Nozomi Okuhara.
Nobel Prize: Indian-born economist Abhijit Banerjee was jointly awarded the 2019 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for his experimental approach to alleviating global poverty.
First Case: On January 30, 2020, India recorded its first official COVID-19 case in Thrissur, Kerala, involving a student returning from Wuhan, China.
Janata Curfew: On March 22, 2020, India observed a voluntary 14-hour nationwide lockdown called by Prime Minister Narendra Modi to prepare the public for social distancing.

Nationwide Lockdown: On March 24, 2020, the Government of India ordered a strict 21-day nationwide lockdown for its 1.3 billion citizens. This was subsequently extended in multiple phases through May.

Migrant Exodus: The abrupt halt of transport and economic activity triggered a humanitarian crisis, prompting 40 million migrant workers to travel thousands of kilometers back to their hometowns on foot or via special trains.
Economic Relief: The government launched the Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan (Self-Reliant India Movement) in May to inject economic stimulus and structural reforms into a heavily impacted market.

Galwan Valley Clash: Tensions peaked along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in eastern Ladakh. During the night of June 15–16, 2020, a violent hand-to-hand combat in the Galwan Valley resulted in the deaths of 20 Indian Army personnel.

Chinese App Ban: In response to border escalations and security concerns, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology banned 59 popular Chinese mobile applications, including TikTok, WeChat, and CamScanner.
UN Security Council: On June 17, 2020, India was elected as a non-permanent member of the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) for a two-year term starting in January 2021.

Bodo Peace Accord: On January 27, 2020, the Government of India signed a historic tripartite agreement with the Government of Assam and Bodo representatives, successfully ending a 50-year-old extremist crisis.
Delhi Riots: In late February 2020, severe communal violence erupted in Northeast Delhi amid tensions surrounding the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA), resulting in over 40 casualties.

Agricultural Farm Laws: In September 2020, Parliament passed three contentious agricultural reform bills. This sparked widespread, long-term protests and blockades by farmer unions at the borders of New Delhi.

Ram Mandir Foundation: On August 5, 2020, Prime Minister Narendra Modi laid the foundation stone for the construction of the Ram Janmabhoomi temple in Ayodhya, following the 2019 Supreme Court verdict.
Cyclone Amphan: In May 2020, an extremely severe cyclonic storm hit West Bengal and parts of Odisha, causing massive structural damage and claiming dozens of lives.
Vizag Gas Leak: A hazardous styrene gas leak occurred at the LG Polymers chemical plant near Visakhapatnam on May 7, 2020, resulting in over 10 fatalities and thousands falling ill.

Air India Express Flight 1344: On August 7, 2020, a repatriation flight operating under the Vande Bharat Mission overshot the tabletop runway at Calicut International Airport in Kerala, breaking apart and killing 21 people.
Nirbhaya Case Verdict: After years of legal delays, the four convicts of the 2012 Delhi gang-rape and murder case were executed by hanging at Tihar Jail on March 20, 2020.

Babri Masjid Demolition Case: On September 30, 2020, a special CBI court acquitted all 32 accused individuals—including veteran political figures like L.K. Advani and Murli Manohar Joshi—citing a lack of conclusive evidence regarding a pre-planned conspiracy.
India officially began its two-year tenure as a non-permanent member of the United Nations Security Council (UNSC).
The Drug Controller General of India approved emergency use authorization for two COVID-19 vaccines: Covishield (Oxford/AstraZeneca produced by Serum Institute) and Covaxin (Bharat Biotech).
India launched the world’s largest COVID-19 vaccination drive, initially targeting healthcare and frontline workers.
On Republic Day, the year-long farmers' protests escalated as a tractor rally breached the Red Fort in New Delhi, leading to widespread clashes.
A catastrophic glacier burst in the Chamoli district of Uttarakhand triggered severe flash floods down the Rishiganga and Dhauliganga rivers, leaving over 200 people dead or missing.
The Motera Stadium in Ahmedabad was renamed the Narendra Modi Stadium, becoming the largest cricket stadium in the world.

April – May: India was struck by a devastating second wave of COVID-19 driven by the Delta variant. The surge overwhelmed the healthcare system, leading to critical, country-wide shortages of medical oxygen and hospital beds.
Phase 3 of the vaccination drive opened up eligibility to all citizens above the age of 18.
Cyclone Tauktae, an extremely severe cyclonic storm, struck the western coast of India, causing heavy casualties and damage in Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Goa.
Days after Tauktae, Cyclone Yaas hit the eastern coast, devastating coastal areas of Odisha and West Bengal.
Legendary Indian sprinter Milkha Singh (famously known as the "Flying Sikh") passed away at age 91 due to COVID-19 complications.
Dilip Kumar, one of the greatest icons of Hindi cinema, passed away at the age of 98.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi executed a massive Cabinet overhaul, introducing 36 new faces and seeing high-profile exits, including Health Minister Harsh Vardhan and IT Minister Ravi Shankar Prasad.
Neeraj Chopra won a historic Gold Medal in Men's Javelin Throw at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, securing India’s first-ever Olympic gold medal in track and field.
The Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award, India's highest sporting honor, was officially renamed the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award.
Tata Sons won the competitive bidding process to acquire national carrier Air India for ₹18,000 crore, bringing the airline back to its original founders after 68 years.
India crossed a monumental public health milestone by administering 1 billion (100 crore) COVID-19 vaccine doses.

In a major political reversal on Guru Nanak Jayanti, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the repeal of the three controversial farm laws, leading to the official end of the year-long farmers' blockade around Delhi.
Parag Agrawal, an IIT Bombay alumnus, was appointed as the new Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Twitter.
India's first Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), General Bipin Rawat, his wife, and 11 other military personnel tragically lost their lives when their Mi-17V5 helicopter crashed in Coonoor, Tamil Nadu.
India’s Harnaaz Sandhu was crowned Miss Universe 2021 in Eilat, Israel, bringing the title back to India after 21 years.
First Tribal Woman President: Droupadi Murmu made history by assuming office as the 15th President of India.

State Legislative Elections: The BJP won key assembly elections across 6 out of 7 states (including Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Goa, and Manipur), while the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) registered a landslide victory in Punjab.
Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav: The country marked 75 years of Indian independence with mass public campaigns like Har Ghar Tiranga.
The Agnipath Scheme: A new short-term military recruitment system was launched, triggering widespread student and youth protests across several states.
Abortion Law Liberalization: In a landmark verdict, the Supreme Court ruled that all women—regardless of marital status—are legally entitled to safe abortions up to 24 weeks.
50th Chief Justice: Justice D.Y. Chandrachud took oath as the Chief Justice of India.
Hijab Ban Upheld: The Karnataka High Court upheld restrictions on religious attire in schools, ruling that wearing the hijab is not an essential religious practice under Islam.
Indigenous Military Capabilities: India commissioned its first home-built aircraft carrier, INS Vikrant, significantly expanding its naval sovereignty.
Private Space Boom: Skyroot Aerospace launched Vikram-S, marking India's first successful privately developed rocket mission into space.
The 5G Rollout: The government successfully executed a massive 5G spectrum auction grossing over ₹1.5 lakh crore, paving the way for the high-speed telecom revolution across major cities.
Morbi Bridge Collapse: A British-era suspension bridge in Gujarat tragically collapsed over the Machchhu River, claiming 135 lives.

Extreme Weather Waves: Northern parts of the country experienced breaking heatwaves that affected staple crop yields, while record-breaking monsoon cloudbursts caused devastating floods in Assam and Uttarakhand.
Historic Chess Olympiad: For the very first time, India hosted the 44th FIDE Chess Olympiad in Chennai.
Pay Parity in Cricket: The BCCI announced an equal-pay policy, offering identical match fees to both men and women international cricket players.

Wrestlers' Protest: Prominent Indian wrestlers (including Vinesh Phogat, Sakshi Malik, and Bajrang Punia) protested at Jantar Mantar against Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh over sexual harassment allegations.
Delhi Excise Policy: Deputy Chief Minister Manish Sisodia was arrested by the CBI regarding irregularities in the scrapped Delhi excise policy.
Weather Extremes: Central India recorded a 99% rainfall deficit (the worst in 122 years).
Rahul Gandhi Disqualification: Rahul Gandhi was disqualified from the Lok Sabha following a criminal defamation conviction.
Assembly Elections: The BJP won the Tripura Assembly elections and returned to power in Meghalaya and Nagaland as a coalition partner.
Population Milestone: India officially surpassed China to become the world’s most populous country, estimated at 142.86 crore.
Atiq Ahmed Killed: Gangster-turned-politician Atiq Ahmed and his brother Ashraf were shot dead live on television by assailants posing as journalists in Prayagraj.
Lithium Reserves: Large reserves of lithium were discovered in Jammu and Kashmir.
Manipur Clashes: Ethnic and violent clashes broke out in Manipur following a Tribal Solidarity March, resulting in widespread displacement and casualties.
New Parliament Building: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the new Parliament building in New Delhi.
Odisha Train Collision: A tragic three-train crash occurred in Balasore, Odisha, causing massive loss of life and injuries.
France-India Ties: PM Narendra Modi attended Bastille Day celebrations in France as the Guest of Honour.
Chandrayaan-3: ISRO successfully landed the Chandrayaan-3 Vikram lander on the South Pole of the Moon, making India the first nation to do so.
Haryana Violence: Communal violence flared up in Nuh district of Haryana during a VHP-led procession.
G20 Summit: India successfully hosted the G20 Leaders' Summit in New Delhi under the theme "Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam" ("One Earth, One Family, One Future").
Women’s Reservation Bill: Parliament passed the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (Women's Reservation Bill), reserving 33% of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies.
Aditya-L1: ISRO launched Aditya-L1, India's first space-based solar observatory mission to study the sun.
Article 370: The Supreme Court of India delivered a landmark verdict unanimously upholding the abrogation of Article 370 in Jammu and Kashmir.
Silkyara Tunnel Rescue: All 41 trapped construction workers were safely rescued after 17 days following a tunnel collapse in Uttarkashi, Uttarakhand.
Cricket World Cup: India reached the final of the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023, finishing as runners-up after losing to Australia

18th Lok Sabha Elections: Held between April and June, registering a record-breaking 642 million voters (including 312 million women). Prime Minister Narendra Modi took the oath of office for a historic third consecutive term, leading a coalition government under the NDA banner.
Jammu & Kashmir Assembly Elections: Conducted for the first time in a decade following the abrogation of Article 370, resulting in the formation of a new alliance government.
Electoral Bonds Verdict: In February, a unanimous landmark judgment by a constitutional bench of the Supreme Court of India struck down the Electoral Bond Scheme as unconstitutional and arbitrary.
Uniform Civil Code (UCC): Uttarakhand became the first state in independent India to pass a Uniform Civil Code bill.

Judicial Overhaul: The three new criminal justice laws—Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam—officially replaced the colonial-era IPC, CrPC, and Indian Evidence Act.

XPoSat & Aditya-L1: ISRO commenced the year by launching the X-ray Polarimeter Satellite (XPoSat) to study black holes, followed quickly by successfully inserting the Aditya-L1 spacecraft into Lagrange Point 1 to observe the solar corona.
GaganYaan Milestone: ISRO officially announced and introduced the four chosen astronaut-designates for India’s premier human spaceflight mission.
Meteorological Advancements: The launch of the INSAT-3DS satellite in February substantially enhanced the country's weather forecasting, storm warning, and climate monitoring capabilities.
Atal Setu Inauguration: India's longest sea bridge, the Mumbai Trans Harbour Link (Atal Setu), spanning 21.8 km, was officially opened to public transit.
Macroeconomic Resilience: India maintained its status as the world’s fastest-growing major economy, with GDP growth hovering near 6.5–7% alongside stable, low core inflation.
Digital Infrastructure Boost: Unified Payments Interface (UPI) volumes breached record-setting peaks, exceeding 16.58 billion transactions in a single month.
Green Energy Expansion: Construction escalated on the Khavda Renewable Energy Park in Gujarat, cementing its trajectory to become the world’s largest hybrid solar-wind installation.
T20 World Cup Triumph: The Indian Men's Cricket Team won the ICC T20 World Cup in June, remaining completely undefeated throughout the tournament and breaking an 11-year ICC trophy drought.
Youngest World Chess Champion: 18-year-old Grandmaster D. Gukesh won the FIDE Candidates Tournament and subsequently clinched the World Chess Championship title.
Paris 2024 Olympics: India concluded its campaign with 6 medals, highlighted by shooter Manu Bhaker becoming the first Indian athlete since Independence to win two medals at a single Olympic edition.

Ram Mandir Pran Pratishtha: The formal consecration ceremony of the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya took place in January, marking a major cultural shift and driving massive tourism infrastructure growth in Uttar Pradesh.
Delhi Assembly Elections (February): The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) won a decisive majority in the Delhi Legislative Assembly, securing 48 out of 70 seats.
Manipur Political Shift (February): Following persistent ethnic tensions, Chief Minister N. Biren Singh resigned, leading to the temporary imposition of President's Rule.
Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025: Parliament passed controversial legislative amendments to the Waqf Act, prompting nationwide public debate and localized protests, notably in West Bengal.
Judicial Transitions (November): Justice Surya Kant was sworn in as the 52nd Chief Justice of India (CJI), succeeding Justice B.R. Gavai.
Bihar Assembly Elections (November): The BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) secured a landslide victory, winning 202 out of 243 seats.
Union Budget 2025–26: The government announced a major structural update, offering a complete income tax rebate for earnings up to ₹12 Lakh per annum under the new tax regime.

Semiconductor Breakthrough (September): India presented its first functional batch of "Made in India" semiconductor microchips to Prime Minister Modi, completing a rapid 3.5-year cycle from policy approval to physical fabrication.
GST Rate Overhaul (September): The GST Council compressed tax slabs into a simplified system (primarily 5%, 18%, and a 40% sin tax), which pushed collections to record highs.
Monetary Policy Easing: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) cut the repo rate by a cumulative 125 basis points over four consecutive cycles, lowering it to 5.25%.

Operation Sindoor (May): Following a tragic terror strike in Pahalgam that claimed 26 lives, the Indian Armed Forces executed cross-border counter-terrorism strikes against camp infrastructures. A temporary bilateral military de-escalation ceasefire followed later in the month.

Left-Wing Extremism Drawdown: The Ministry of Home Affairs reported a historic reduction in the operational footprint of Left-Wing Extremism (LWE), with active high-violence zones falling to just 11 districts nationwide.
US Tariff Fractures (August): The newly formed US administration imposed blanket 25% tariffs on Indian goods, escalating later to secondary penalties aimed at capping Indian imports of Russian crude.

Space Docking Success (January): ISRO successfully executed the SPADEEX mission, docking two individual satellites in orbit—a milestone enabling autonomous space power transfers and laying the groundwork for the future Bhartiya Antariksh Station.

Anji Khad & Chenab Rail Bridges (April): India's first cable-stayed railway bridge (Anji Khad) and the world's highest railway bridge (Chenab) were fully integrated into the Udhampur–Srinagar–Baramulla Rail Link (USBRL) network.
Aviation Expansion: Phase 1 operations officially commenced at both the Noida International Airport (Jewar) and the Navi Mumbai International Airport, dramatically reducing historical hub congestion.

Maha Kumbh Mela (January–February): The historic Prayagraj congregation drew over 660 million devotees to the Triveni Sangam. However, the gathering faced significant crowd-control issues, including a tragic crush that claimed over 30 lives.
ICC Men's Champions Trophy (March): The Indian Men's Cricket team lifted the Champions Trophy after defeating New Zealand in a tense final in Dubai.
ICC Women's Cricket World Cup (November): The Indian Women's Cricket team clinched their historic, maiden ODI World Cup title.
Cricket Retirement (May): Legendary batsman Virat Kohli officially announced his retirement from Test Cricket.
Air India Flight 171 Tragedy (June): An Air India flight crashed shortly after takeoff from Ahmedabad Airport, resulting in 260 fatalities including people on the ground.

Aviation Crew Crisis (December): IndiGo Airlines was forced to cancel over 4,500 flights within a 10-day period following scheduling failures linked to strict compliance with the DGCA's updated Flight Duty Time Limitations (FDTL).

Environmental Strain: Northern India, particularly Delhi-NCR, suffered its worst recorded winter air pollution crisis, with prolonged periods where the Air Quality Index (AQI) continuously maxed out at 500

Republic Day & Chief Guests: India celebrated its 77th Republic Day on January 26, 2026, with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa as chief guests.
Independence Day Theme: The 80th Independence Day on August 15, 2026, was observed under the theme "150 Years of Vande Mataram" and "Yuva Shakti for Viksit Bharat@2047".
Aadhaar Mascot: The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) launched the official Aadhaar mascot 'Udai' on January 8, 2026.
Paperless Judiciary: Kerala inaugurated India's first fully paperless district judiciary in Kalpetta.
Economic Growth: India's real GDP growth for 2026 is projected around 6.9% by major analysts like Goldman Sachs.
Wholesale Inflation: India's wholesale inflation reached an 49-month high of 11.39% by mid-October 2026.

Trade & Manufacturing: India's exports to China experienced a 40% growth with the trade deficit crossing $100 billion. India also emerged as the first country to commercially produce bio-bitumen for sustainable road construction.
Energy & Tech: India Energy Week 2026 took place in Goa (January 27–30), and the AI Impact Summit India 2026 was held in February 2026 alongside regional AI conferences in Rajasthan.
Wetlands & Biodiversity: Two new wetlands were officially designated as Ramsar sites in October 2026. A new reed snake species (Calamaria mizoramensis) was also discovered in Mizoram.
Jnanpith Award: Vairamuthu was selected for the 60th Jnanpith Award, following Vinod Kumar Shukla who received the 59th Jnanpith Award.
International Achievements: India secured four gold medals at the International Chemistry Olympiad 2026
